title: DELETE /v1/budgets/{id} deletes an organization-owned budget and silently uncaps its users
body:
Noted in review on #898. Pre-existing, and a sibling of #881 rather than part of it.

## What is open

`DELETE /v1/budgets/{id}` (`src/gateway/api/routes/budgets.py`) resolves the budget by id with no ownership predicate, so a deployment operator can delete an organization-owned budget. The route refuses with a 409 while a workspace default or a spend ceiling names it, which are the two RESTRICT foreign keys, but neither check is about ownership and neither covers the tenant's other rows:

- `users.budget_id` is not checked at all. `Budget.users` is a plain relationship, so the ORM nulls the column out and any gateway user on that budget loses their cap with nobody told. This is the same shape #875 fixed on the organization-scoped delete, which counts those rows and refuses; the deployment route never got the matching guard.
- `budget_reset_logs.budget_id` is NOT NULL behind a plain relationship, so a budget that has ever reset fails the null-out at the commit and the caller gets a 500 "Database error" rather than a refusal naming anything.

From the tenant's side, a budget they defined disappears from their Spend page with no record of who removed it, and any ceiling that named it is gone with it.

The dashboard reaches it: since #898 the operator's Budgets page labels a tenant's row "Owned by an organization" and still offers Delete on it, individually and through the bulk bar.

## Suggested fix

Two separable decisions:

1. Whether the deployment surface may delete a tenant's budget at all. Refusing is the consistent answer with #881 and #875, but note that `PATCH /v1/budgets/{id}` deliberately still reaches those rows (it retimes their ceilings), so "the operator may edit but not delete" needs saying out loud if that is the choice.
2. The `users` and `budget_reset_logs` holds, which are a bug on this route regardless of ownership: a delete that silently uncaps a user, or answers 500 on a budget that has reset, is wrong on the deployment's own budgets too.

(2) is worth doing whichever way (1) goes.

title: Class names mentioned in foundation.test.ts become working utilities in the shipped bundle
body:
Measured on `d894843f`, against the CSS the dashboard build emits.

`web/src/styles/foundation.test.ts` is the guard that fails a raw hex, a numbered Tailwind palette class, or a hand-rolled type role anywhere under `web/src`. Every class name the test itself mentions becomes a real, working utility in the shipped bundle, which means the guard cannot fail on the thing it exists to catch: a call site using one of those names would render correctly instead of failing visibly.

Tailwind v4 automatic source detection is in use. There is no `@source` directive in `globals.css` and no Tailwind config file, so every file in the project is scanned for class-name candidates, `*.test.ts` included.

## Known instances

- `border-emerald-200`, in the comment at line 606 that lists Tailwind's numbered palette as the thing the test forbids. `.border-emerald-200` is in the shipped CSS.
- `text-emphasis`, in the role-name array at line 744 and in the assertion message at line 1001. `.text-emphasis` is in the shipped CSS even though the role has no call site anywhere in `web/src`.

Note that only the first of these is a comment. The other two sites are a string array and an assertion message that the test legitimately needs, so rewording prose does not fix this.

The secondary cost is bytes, plus the oddity of shipping a numbered-palette class that this very test exists to forbid.

## Suggested fix

Exclude test files from source detection, either with an `@source not` rule covering `*.test.ts` and `*.test.tsx` or with an explicit `@source` naming the application sources. Then confirm both known rules are gone from the built CSS.

One cause, and these two are the known symptoms. Sweeping for others belongs to this fix rather than to a separate one.

title: The three credential stores stage writes for their routes and re-encrypt without a version check
body:
`provider_store_service`, `search_tool_store_service` and `guardrail_store_service` share one shape, and two review findings on #1120 are really findings about that shape. Both apply to all three equally, which is why neither belongs in a PR that touches only the newest one.

## Transaction ownership

`src/gateway/AGENTS.md` says "Services own commits and rollbacks." These three do not: `save_*` and `delete_*` stage mutations and say so in their docstrings ("staged; caller commits"), leaving the route to call `db.commit()` and to map an `IntegrityError` to a 409.

There is a reason it ended up this way. The route needs the commit to fail in its own hands so it can turn a primary-key collision into a 409 with a resource-specific message, and it needs the write and the cache refresh that follows to be ordered. But the convention and the code disagree, and right now the code wins three times over. Either the services should own their transactions and hand back something a route can turn into a 409, or the convention should record this as the deliberate exception it has become.

## Re-encryption without a version check

`reencrypt_*` reads every row holding a secret, decrypts, re-encrypts and lets the ORM flush. Nothing pins the write to the ciphertext that was read. A PATCH committing between the read and the flush is overwritten with a re-encryption of the value it replaced.

The window is small and the operation is rare, run by hand during a key rotation. It is also not guarded at all today: `with_for_update()` is not used on this path, and SQLite would not emit `FOR UPDATE` if it were. A conditional update matching the original ciphertext, treating zero rows as "someone else got there first", would close it.

## Why this was deferred

Raised in review on #1120: https://github.com/mozilla-ai/otari/pull/1120#discussion_r4003504339 and https://github.com/mozilla-ai/otari/pull/1120#discussion_r4003504347

Changing one store to answer them would leave three stores with two shapes, which is worse than three stores with one flawed shape: the next person copies whichever they find first. Both points want a single change across all three.

title: Add price_per_call for managed tool pricing
body:
## Desired behavior

Accept `price_per_call` in YAML pricing entries for gateway-managed tools, expressed in USD per successful invocation. Keep the existing token-price fields for LLM models.

```yaml
pricing:
  otari:web_fetch:
    price_per_call: 0.001
  otari:web_search:
    price_per_call: 0.001
  otari:code_execution:
    price_per_call: 0.001
```

## Why

Managed Search and code execution already reuse `input_price_per_million` for USD per million successful calls; Fetch follows the same convention. A value of `1000` therefore means $0.001 per call, not a model-agnostic input-token rate. The unused `output_price_per_million` field makes this harder to understand. The dashboard already accepts dollars per call.

Fetch/Search tool charges remain separate from the selected model's token charges, including the cost of reading retrieved content.

## Notes

- **Backward compatibility:** continue accepting existing YAML unchanged, including its legacy output-price field, with identical billing. Treat `price_per_call` as an additive config option, not a rename or removal of existing fields. Reject an entry mixing it with either legacy input/output pricing field, even if values agree, with an actionable configuration error. Different entries may use different formats.
- **Storage and API:** convert `price_per_call × 1,000,000` to the existing internal input-rate representation using decimal-safe arithmetic. No database migration or pricing API contract change is required. Preserve existing stored prices, historical usage, API clients, dashboard behavior, and database-over-YAML precedence.
- **Validation and billing:** accept finite nonnegative rates, including explicit zero; reject negative/non-finite rates and use on LLM pricing entries. Preserve `require_pricing` behavior: a missing tool price is rejected when enabled, while explicit zero is configured free pricing. Failed tool invocations remain unbilled; model token pricing is unchanged.
- **Verification and docs:** test legacy/new-format charge equivalence, fractional and zero rates, conflicting fields, invalid rates, model-entry rejection, and existing-database precedence. Update config examples and tool pricing docs to state USD per successful call and explain compatibility with the old format.

Keep this separate from the Web Fetch stack. Search and code execution support can land independently; include Fetch when its activation is available.

Ref: #813, #979, #1017

title: An API key's model listing does not flag hosted models as deployment-managed
body:
### Problem

`GET /api/v1/models` sets `deployment_managed` on each model. For a dashboard session, a hosted model is flagged when the deployment pays for it in at least one of the organization's workspaces. That is the same rule the organization rate-override gate uses.

For an API key, `catalog_scope` passes an empty set of hosted providers, so a hosted model always reads `deployment_managed: false`. An API key belongs to a workspace, so its organization is known, and the rate-override gate applies to that organization. A client that reads the flag from an API-key listing is told the organization may set its own rate for a model where the gateway refuses that rate.

`GET /api/v1/models/{model_id}` and `GET /api/v1/catalog/models` build their scope the same way, so they have the same gap.

### Decision

`deployment_managed` has one meaning on every path: the organization may not set its own rate for this model. That is the rule the rate-override gate applies, so an API key's listing follows the session rule.

### Fix

On the API-key path of `catalog_scope` (`services/merged_catalog_service.py`), use the key's organization to compute the deployment-supplied providers as the session path does: the bound `ModelProviderPort`'s hosted providers minus `OrgProviderKeyService.get_byo_providers`. A master key stays unflagged, because an operator may price any model. Replace the code comment that says an API key's hosted models stay unflagged, and give the field a description in the public schema.

### Acceptance

- [ ] An API key's listing, single-model read and grouped catalog flag a hosted model exactly where a session in the same organization does.
- [ ] A test checks the API-key flag against the organization rate-override write for the same model.
- [ ] A master key's listing flags no hosted model.
- [ ] `deployment_managed` has a description in `docs/public/openapi.json`, and the generated artifacts are regenerated.

title: Routing fallback dropdown fails to load model choices
body: ## What happens When adding a model fallback to a routing policy, the dropdown shows no model choices and instead displays: > The model list could not be read. Type the selector; it is sent exactly as typed either way. Observed in a user-provided screenshot of the “Fallback 3” field. `web/src/features/models/ModelComboBox.tsx` displays this message when the model-list query errors. The failing request, HTTP status, deployment mode, and root cause are not yet confirmed. ## Expected The fallback dropdown lists available models while still allowing a manually entered `provider:model` selector. ## Repro 1. Open the routing policy form in the dashboard. 2. Add a fallback and open its model dropdown. 3. In the reported session, the dropdown displays the error above instead of model choices. Not independently reproduced. Related: #1260 (closed, hosted model visibility) and #876 (open, failed organization-context reads). Neither is confirmed to explain this failure.

title: Models page filters the catalog in the browser, so it is bounded by one request
body:
## What

`useCatalog` fetches the whole catalog in one request and `ModelCatalogPage` does the rest in the browser: the filter rail's facets, the provider count, the sort, the search and the pagination footer are all computed from what that one response carried.

That was fine while a catalog was whatever `config.providers` dialed plus whatever had a deployment price row. It is not fine now: an organization adopting one BYO provider key offers over a hundred models by itself, and a local single-provider deployment already reached 126.

## Where it stands

The request asked for the endpoint's default window of 100 and silently described that window as though it were the catalog. That is fixed: it asks for the maximum (1000) and the page says so when `count` exceeds what arrived, so a truncated catalog is visible rather than silent.

A bigger number is not the answer, though. The page is still bounded by one request, and every facet it draws still describes what fits in it.

## What would fix it

Move the filtering, the sort and the facet counts to the server, and page against it.

- `GET /api/v1/catalog/models` already takes `skip`, `limit` and `search`, and already returns `count` (matches before the window). `useCatalogSearch` uses that path for the model picker, which is where otari#1380 put search server-side for the same reason.
- What it does not have is the facets: the filter rail needs counts per provider, per capability and per price source over the *whole* matching set, not over a page. That is the part that needs a new response shape, and it is the reason this is an issue rather than a patch.

## Not a workaround

Raising the limit again, or raising the endpoint's `le=1000` ceiling, moves the cliff without removing it, and makes the browser hold more of a table it should be asking the server about.

title: feat(guardrails): let an organization mandate name a hosted guardrail
body:
Part of #1643.

Let an organization mandate name a hosted guardrail. Add `organization_guardrails.hosted_guardrail_id` (indexed, no foreign key: the table belongs to an overlay). A mandate names at most one of `url`, `definition_id`, and `hosted_guardrail_id`, and a hosted mandate carries no credential.

The migration rebuilds the table SQLite-safely, as `a9c4e7b2d5f8` does. Create and update check through the port that the organization may pick the guardrail, and answer 404 otherwise.

title: feat(guardrails): add the mandate listing and evaluation service a hybrid peer serves
body:
Part of #1643.

Add a core service in `services/tenancy/` that a hybrid peer calls to serve the new protocol: list a workspace's mandates as descriptors, and evaluate a set of mandate ids for one request. Definitions run on the control plane's runner, remote mandates use the organization's URL and credential, and hosted ones go through the port only when the caller allows it.

This also closes the gap where an organization's own guardrails are never enforced on a hybrid gateway.

title: One MCP resolution error covers six conditions, and none of them logs
body:
## What

`McpServerResolutionFailedError` is raised at nine sites in `src/gateway/adapters/mcp_server_adapter.py`, for seven distinct conditions:

- a scope naming no workspace, in the local adapter (twice)
- a scope holding no token, in the remote adapter
- a peer answer that is not an object
- a `servers` value that is not a list
- a peer answering several entries for one requested ID
- an entry whose ID does not match the one requested
- an entry the model cannot validate (twice)

The fixed public message is correct: the underlying detail quotes the stored server URL and its credential, so it must not travel. But the error carries nothing else either, so an operator looking at a 502 has nothing that tells the nine apart.

## Why it matters

A hybrid gateway returning `MCP server resolution failed` gives the operator no way to tell a peer that answered badly from a gateway that was wired wrong. The two have different owners and different fixes.

## Suggested shape

A required, typed `reason` on the error, named at each raise site. The wire response does not change, and no reason names any part of the peer's answer. #1738 does this and nothing more.

Recording the reason is a separate problem, because a failure's record belongs where its response is produced and neither surface does both. On this router, `_McpRoute.handler` renders the error response and writes no log, while the route handlers log the outcome and re-raise so it can render. On the completions path there is no `HTTPException` handler and no middleware log at all. #1752 covers both surfaces, and this issue closes once that lands.

Not a `logger.warning` beside each raise, and not one at each handling boundary either. Both are log-and-raise: they put the choice of how loud a condition is in code that cannot know whether a caller recovers from it, and they leave the cause reachable only by scraping log text. `McpExecutionError` in `src/gateway/services/mcp_stateless.py` is the local pattern for carrying a cause, holding a code and an execution state rather than a message.

## Notes

Found while reviewing #1683. Deliberately left out of it: that change's acceptance criterion is identical behavior in all three modes, and adding log lines is new behavior.

title: Add FileAuthorityPort, so a data plane with no database can serve files
body:
### Problem

A hybrid data plane holds no database, so file metadata, authorization and lifecycle state have nowhere local to live. #1606 settles that they live on the control plane and are reached across a network boundary.

That boundary is a port. Today `services/files/` reaches repositories directly, which is correct for standalone and has no hybrid answer at all.

### Proposal

Add `ports/file_authority_port.py` and a core HTTP adapter under `adapters/`, following `ports/mcp_server_port.py` and its adapter as the worked example.

The port carries metadata and authorization commands, never file bytes and never storage credentials. Its command groups are the ones the wire contract sets out: uploads, reads, copies and outputs, deletion, and readiness.

`FilesService` keeps one set of use cases and gains two bindings. A local binding receives the request's repositories and Unit of Work. A remote binding receives this port and has neither. The builder rejects an invalid combination, so no route chooses an implementation.

Follow the existing pattern in `api/deps.py`: a getter beside the others, an annotated alias in the alias block, and the alias in `__all__`. A `build_*_port` helper raises a plain `ValueError` naming the condition it cannot serve, as `build_file_storage_port` does. Only `container.py` names the concrete adapter, and its binding carries a comment saying what the core default does.

### Done when

- [ ] The port exists with no import of services or API schemas.
- [ ] One `FilesService` serves both bindings, with no second hybrid service.
- [ ] Nothing on the request path asks which mode it is running in.

title: Store the digests of API keys and tokens as HMAC under a pepper per purpose
body:
### Problem

Otari stores the digests it checks secrets against as plain SHA-256: API keys (`auth/models.py`), the master key (`services/master_key_service.py`), dashboard sessions (`services/dashboard_session_service.py`), organization and verification tokens (`services/tenancy/tokens.py`, `services/tenancy/organization_service.py`), and OAuth state (`services/oauth_service.py`). The security review instructions state it as the rule: "API keys are stored as one-way SHA-256 hashes, never as plaintext."

A plain digest has two weaknesses a keyed one does not:

- anyone holding a copy of the database can test a guessed value offline, with no other secret;
- one value hashes to the same digest in every deployment, so two databases can be linked.

Otari's own API keys are long random values, so guessing one is impractical today. The gain is defense in depth, and it matters most for the lower-entropy values on the list.

#1666 names the provider account a file copy is in with HMAC-SHA256 under `OTARI_PROVIDER_ACCOUNT_PEPPER`, a secret kept for that one purpose. The same pattern fits every digest above.

### Proposal

Store each digest as HMAC-SHA256 under a pepper kept for its own purpose (for example `OTARI_API_KEY_HASH_PEPPER` and `OTARI_SESSION_HASH_PEPPER`), with these rules:

- each pepper is required where its feature is on, at least 32 characters, and different from every other pepper, `OTARI_SECRET_KEY` and the master key, checked at startup;
- each purpose has its own pepper, so a leak of one exposes nothing else and each rotates on its own cadence;
- the docs state what rotating each one costs (for example, rotating the API key pepper invalidates every stored key, and rotating the session pepper signs every dashboard user out);
- comparisons stay constant-time (`hmac.compare_digest`).

Existing rows need a migration path, because an API key's plaintext is never stored and its digest cannot be recomputed. A digest version per row allows both during a transition: a key that verifies against the legacy SHA-256 digest is rewritten with the keyed one, and the legacy path is removed after a stated window.

Update the rule in `.github/instructions/security-review.instructions.md` and the backend standards skill in the same change.

### Acceptance

- [ ] No digest of a secret value is stored unkeyed.
- [ ] Startup refuses a missing, short or shared pepper, and the message never contains the value.
- [ ] Existing API keys keep working through the transition, and a test covers the upgrade of a legacy row.
- [ ] The docs list each pepper, where it is required, and what rotating it costs.

title: docs: add the Deploy on Railway button to README.md and docs/deployment.md, refresh the Railway steps
body:
### What

`deploy/railway/template.json` and `deploy/railway/README.md` both say the deploy link is "the Deploy on Railway button in README.md", and the README's maintenance notes say to update the button "here, in the project root `README.md`, and in `docs/deployment.md`". Neither the root `README.md` nor `docs/deployment.md` has a button; both only link the `deploy/railway/README.md` page in a sentence. The Render template has the same gap.

Also in `deploy/railway/README.md`:

- Step 3 ("Generate a public domain") looks already handled by the template (the test deploy came with a domain); confirm and drop or reword.
- The configuration table should gain `PORT` (and `OTARI_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` if the hardening issue lands), each with the one sentence that says why it exists.
- The "Maintaining the template" section should state that the live template lives in the mozilla-ai workspace and name who can edit it, since the 2026-10-01 drift sat unnoticed partly because nobody with repo access had workspace access at hand.

### Why

The button is how most people find the template, and the repo's own files claim it is in two places it is not.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deploy on Railway (and Deploy to Render) buttons in the root `README.md` deployment section and in `docs/deployment.md`'s "Managed deployment templates"
- [ ] `deploy/railway/README.md` steps match what the live template actually does
- [ ] `template.json`'s `_comment` points at the real location of the button

title: A missing row named in a request body answers 404, which says the URL was not found
body:
### Problem

RFC 9110 defines 404 as "the target resource was not found", and the target is the URL. Several write routes answer 404 when the URL exists but an ID in the request body names a row that does not exist. For example, `CreateScopedBudgetRequest.budget_id` gives `OrganizationBudgetNotFoundError`. Others include `DeploymentBudgetNotFoundError`, `EndUserBudgetNotFoundError` and `WorkspaceBudgetDefaultBudgetNotFoundError`. A client cannot tell "this endpoint or parent does not exist" from "a field in your body is wrong".

### Fix

A missing row named in the request body answers 422, and the error names the field. A missing row named in the URL keeps 404.

### Done when

- [ ] Every not-found error raised for a body field is listed, and each answers 422 and names its field.
- [ ] The OpenAPI spec, the Postman collection and `web/src/client/schema.ts` are regenerated.
- [ ] The dashboard handles the new status where it shows these errors.
- [ ] The PR description names the change as a wire change.

title: Status-less InvalidRequestError 400 mapping is too broad under ANY_LLM_UNIFIED_EXCEPTIONS=1
body:
Follow-up to #1006 (fixes #989), from a review thread deferred there.

#1006 maps a status-less `any_llm.exceptions.InvalidRequestError` anywhere in the upstream chain to a client 400 that passes the provider's message through. That is right for the `InvalidRequestError`s any-llm raises natively (gemini, bedrock, deepseek request-shape checks), but the type is only as narrow as whatever assigns it.

With `ANY_LLM_UNIFIED_EXCEPTIONS=1`, any-llm's `convert_exception` picks `InvalidRequestError` by regex (`invalid|badrequest|validation`) over the SDK exception's type name and message (`any_llm/utils/exception_handler.py`). A gateway-side fault with no HTTP status, such as `httpx.InvalidURL` from a misconfigured `api_base` or botocore's `ParamValidationError`, would then reach the caller as a 400 telling them their request was wrong, with upstream text echoed.

Otari does not set the flag today, so this is latent; `src/gateway/api/routes/_platform.py` notes the flag is expected to become any-llm's default, at which point it is live.

Options:
- Narrow the branch to `InvalidRequestError`s any-llm raised itself (for example, no `original_exception`, or one whose original is not a transport/config error).
- Pin the current behavior with a test under `ANY_LLM_UNIFIED_EXCEPTIONS=1` so flipping the default surfaces it.

title: [FEATURE] Attach uploaded files to playground messages
body:
### Problem or use case

Otari already has a Files API (`/api/v1/files`, see `docs/files.md`). A user can upload a file and reference it from a chat request by using its`file_id`. For a text-only local model, Otari extracts the file to text first (#1971).

The playground does not expose any of this. A dashboard user who wants to try document understanding has to leave the playground and use cURL instead.

### Proposed solution

Let a user attach a file to a playground message:

- Attach a file using a button on the UI or drag and drop onto the playground chat window.
- On attach, upload with `POST /api/v1/files` and get back a `file_id`, then send the turn as content parts: the text plus a file part that references the returned `file_id`.
- Show the attachment as a chip on the pending message and in the sent bubble, with its name and size, and a way to remove it before sending.
- Keep the attachment with the turn in saved history, and send it on both sides of a model comparison.
- Show upload errors (size limit, unsupported type) inline in the composer.

Points to decide:

- Visibility. The Files API can be off (it starts disabled when the storage backend cannot be built), and hosted mode does not serve the data plane. The control should show only where uploads work.
- Lifetime. Uploads made from the playground stay in storage after the chat ends. Decide whether to delete them when the chat is cleared, or to list and manage them somewhere.
- Optional: pick from files that were uploaded before (`GET /api/v1/files`), not only new uploads.

### Does this belong in Otari?

Yes. This is a dashboard change over an API that Otari already serves.

title: Allow combining tools in one request
body:
Otari currently rejects a request that uses more than one tool (like MCP, web search and code execution) with "pick one".

We should let one request use multiple tools together, so the model can use them in one run.

title: [FEATURE] Serve /embeddings and the other data-plane routes on a hybrid gateway
body:
### Problem or use case

A gateway in hybrid mode serves only `/chat`, `/messages`, `/responses` and `/mcp`. Every other inference route is absent, so a caller gets a bare `404 Not Found`:

- `/embeddings`
- `/images`
- `/audio`
- `/files`
- `/batches`
- `/rerank`
- `/moderations`
- `/search`
- `/decisions` and `/routing/recommend`

These routes are mounted with `Plane.DATA | Plane.CONTROL` (`src/gateway/api/main.py`, `_CORE_ROUTERS`), so only a standalone deployment serves them. The comment beside them says why: "none of them has hybrid handling".

The hosted control plane refuses the same prefixes (`hosted_mode.DATA_PLANE_PREFIXES`) and tells the caller to send inference to the gateway. In a hybrid plus hosted topology, the request has nowhere to go:

```sh
# hybrid gateway
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8100/api/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OTARI_KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"openai:text-embedding-3-small","input":"hello"}'
# {"detail":"Not Found"}  [404]

# control plane
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8110/api/v1/embeddings ...
# {"detail":"This deployment is a control plane and does not serve inference. Send inference requests to your Otari gateway instead."}  [404]
```

Reproduced on v0.20.0 and on the head of #2220. The route has been standalone-only since the router declaration refactor (#1679, v0.12.0). Before that it was mounted in hybrid mode, but it read the local database and API keys, so it could not have worked there either.

### Proposed solution

Give each of these routes the hybrid handling `/chat` already has:

1. Authorize and get provider credentials from `POST /gateway/provider-keys/resolve`.
2. Call the provider through the resolved attempts.
3. Settle through `POST /gateway/usage` with the unit each route is priced in (tokens, images, seconds, characters, requests).

`/embeddings` is the most requested and is priced per token like a completion, so it is a reasonable first step. Routes that leave durable state (`/files`, `/batches`) need the Try-Confirm/Cancel exchange the protocol describes and could follow separately.

If the resolve or usage contract needs a field for the new routes, document it in `docs/hybrid-mode-protocol.md`, so peers such as the otari-ai overlay can follow.

Until a route has hybrid handling, a hybrid gateway could answer it with a short explanation rather than a bare 404, as the hosted stubs do.

### Does this belong in Otari?

Yes. The hybrid gateway and the wire contract are both Otari's. A peer control plane cannot add these routes to the gateway.

### Alternatives considered

Running a standalone gateway for these routes. That bypasses the control plane's keys, budgets and billing, so it is not an option for a hosted deployment.

title: Docs vs live gateway: base path /v1 vs /api/v1, models list omits a callable model, fresh workspace has no OpenAI provider
body:
Three mismatches found while integrating the hosted gateway (Developers Wilding hackathon, 2026-10-29, fresh workspace). Full notes: https://github.com/Ahmad-glowex/agent-playground/blob/wilding-otari/OTARI.md

**1. Documented base path returns 404**
The Quickstart and blog examples use `https://api.otari.ai/v1`. The live gateway serves `/api/v1` - requests to `/v1/models` return `{"detail": "Otari serves its API under /api/v1, not /v1. Use /api/v1/models instead."}` (the error message itself is excellent, but the docs still point at the old path).

**2. The models list omits models the workspace can call**
`GET /api/v1/models` returned 197 models but did not include `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813`, which the same workspace token calls successfully (including tool calling). It is hard to treat the list as the source of truth for availability.

**3. Fresh workspace: the docs' example provider is not configured**
Calling `openai/gpt-4o-mini` (the README example model) on a fresh workspace returns `provider_not_configured` ("No credential is configured for provider 'openai'"). A working fallback had to be discovered by trial (e.g. `bedrock:amazon.nova-lite-v1:0` works). Either pre-configuring a default provider or noting this in the Quickstart would smooth the first-run experience.

All three are small, but together they made the first hour of integration a guessing game. Happy to provide exact request/response captures.

title: Docs: document regional API hosts for hosted keys (EU keys get 421 on api.otari.ai)
body:
My otari.ai key starts with `otk_v1_eu_`. The docs only show `https://api.otari.ai/api/v1` as the base URL. Requests there are answered `421` "This API key belongs to <host>. Send the request there instead.", and the request then works on `https://eu.api.otari.ai/api/v1`.

OpenAI-compatible SDKs don't follow a 421, so a new user just sees a failed request. I handled it in my app by following the 421 once: https://github.com/ElTanque81/captionwild/blob/main/netlify/lib/otari.mjs

**Suggestion:** list the regional base URLs in the quickstart and API reference, and show the right base URL next to the key in the dashboard when it's created.

(Found while building CaptionWild for Developers Wilding.)

title: [BUG] Hosted quickstart base URL (api.otari.ai/v1) doesn’t match the API (/api/v1, region-specific host)
body:
## Description

Following the hosted quickstart, I used `https://api.otari.ai/v1` as the base URL. That cannot work against the hosted API.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create an API key on the hosted otari.ai platform (my key was in the EU region).
2. Request the model list on the `/v1` URL:

   ```bash
   curl https://api.otari.ai/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>"
   ```

   ```json
   {"detail":"Otari serves its API under /api/v1, not /v1. Use /api/v1/models instead."}
   ```

3. Use `/api/v1`:

   ```bash
   curl https://api.otari.ai/api/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>"
   ```

   ```json
   {"detail":"This API key belongs to eu.api.otari.ai. Send the request there instead."}
   ```

4. Use the region host:

   ```bash
   curl https://eu.api.otari.ai/api/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>"
   ```

   This works.

## Expected behavior

The quickstart and dashboard give a base URL that works: `/api/v1`, on the host for the key's region.

## Suggested fix

- Show the full base URL, including the region host, when a key is created.
- Use `/api/v1` in the quickstart and mention region hosts.

Both error messages were clear and I fixed it in minutes, but the docs sent me to a URL that cannot work.

title: [FEATURE] Let a Fallback policy move on when a candidate refuses with a 200 (content_filter, or unparseable JSON when JSON was requested)
body:
### Problem or use case

Claim Check (built for Devs Wilding: Online) sends every incoming post to a cheap extractor through a Fallback
policy, `cc-extractor`: `meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct` on Bedrock first, `openai/gpt-oss-20b` on DeepInfra second.
The extractor's job is to list the post's factual claims so other agents can check them.

For health-misinformation posts, the first candidate answers **200 OK** with a refusal instead of the JSON it was
asked for, so the policy never moves on:

```
POST /api/v1/chat/completions   model: cc-extractor
post: "Vaccines cause autism and 5G towers spread COVID. Best government ever!"

200  served by us.meta.llama3-1-8b-instruct-v1:0
"I can't fulfill that request. I can't help you spread misinformation about vaccines or COVID-19. ..."
```

The same request sent straight to `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (the policy's second candidate) returns the claims as
asked, every time I tried. `docs/routing.md` says a candidate is skipped on an outage, a rate limit or a 400, so a
refusal that comes back as a normal 200 always stops at the first candidate.

### Proposed solution

An opt-in condition on a Fallback policy (or per candidate), for example `fallback_on: ["refusal"]`, that moves
on to the next candidate when a response is a refusal. Two signals that look cheap to check:

- the provider says so: `finish_reason: "content_filter"`, or a `refusal` field on the message;
- the request asked for `response_format: json_object` / `json_schema` and the reply doesn't parse.

The second signal alone would cover my case, since the client has already said what format it expects. The
`Otari-Fallback` / attempt-count headers could then report the move, as they do for outages today.

### Does this belong in Otari?

I think so: fallback policies are Otari's routing, not a provider parameter, and the decision to try the next
candidate is made in the gateway. The provider call itself (through any-llm) behaves correctly; it's the policy
that has no way to treat a 200 as a failure.

### Alternatives considered

- What I do now: when the reply isn't JSON, retry with `response_format` set. Bedrock rejects JSON mode for that
  model with a 400, so the policy moves on to gpt-oss-20b. It works, but it relies on a provider limitation that
  could go away at any time, and costs a second round trip.
- Retrying from the client against the second model by name. That works too, but then the policy, its Activity
  rows and its headers no longer describe what happened.
- A stricter system prompt ("listing a claim does not endorse it") helps, but not reliably: Llama 3.1 8B still
  refused this post in most of my runs.

Environment: hosted otari.ai, EU region, 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-03.

title: [BUG] /api/v1/models returns chat, embedding, image and rerank models in one list with no capability field
body:
**Otari version:**
Not exposed. /health returns {"status":"healthy"} with no version, and /version, /api/v1/version, /api/v1/health are all 404.
**Python version:**
Not applicable — we call the HTTP API from TypeScript (Node 22). No local Otari process.
**How you're running Otari:** <!-- Docker / docker compose / from source / Railway -->
Managed, at https://otari.ai/api/v1. Not Docker/source/Railway. Auth via Otari-Key header.
**Provider and model:** <!-- e.g. openai:gpt-4o-mini -->
Every model in the catalog — the defect is in /models itself, so no single provider is implicated.
**Reproduces with a direct any-llm call?** <!-- yes / no / haven't tried. Otari dispatches through any-llm; if a plain any_llm call shows the same behavior, please file it at mozilla-ai/any-llm instead. Minimal repro snippet: https://github.com/mozilla-ai/otari/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-this-an-otari-change-or-an-any-llm-change -->
No, and it can't: this is the catalog surface a client reads before dispatch. any-llm is never reached.

We are building an adversarial benchmark for treasury agents: one written policy, several models defending it, another model attacking it, and a separate judge scoring each exchange. Before a run we pick the model roster programmatically from /api/v1/models. That works, except that the list does not say what each model is for, so the only way to find out is to spend a request and get rejected.

title: [BUG] A 504 says "All upstream providers timed out" when the first candidate failed with a 400
body:
**Otari version:** hosted otari.ai, EU (2026-11-01)
**Python version:** n/a (hosted)
**How you're running Otari:** hosted otari.ai, workspace API key
**Provider and model:** routing policy `faber-verify`: main Mistral `mistral-small-2603`, `on_failure` `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (DeepInfra)
**Reproduces with a direct any-llm call?** no (routing message)

### What happened

`504 {"detail":"All upstream providers timed out"}` with `Otari-Error-Retryable: true`, request IDs `1ff48ef4-82ff-4891-ab57-9dbf121f7568` and `4c0dce3a-b459-4bdd-b5e3-ae1a42f5c2fb`. The dashboard trace for `4c0dce3a…` shows:
- #1 `mistral` failed with **400** after 102 ms: the Mistral SDK has no `seed` argument.
- #2 `gpt-oss-120b` on DeepInfra failed with **504** after 8.19 s.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use the policy above.
2. `POST /api/v1/chat/completions` with `{"model":"faber-verify","max_tokens":200,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"In one sentence, what does a small local bakery gain from having a website?"}],"seed":7}`

Whether candidate #2 times out depends on DeepInfra at the time. The message wording is the issue.

### What you expected

A message that matches the attempts, for example "The last candidate timed out after 8.2 s; 1 earlier candidate refused the request (400)". As written, a caller retries a request that will fail the same way on candidate #1.

### Relevant config (redacted)

Routing policy set in the dashboard, as above.
